decomposition_notes: Four goals, one for each requested seam: (1) Organizations and org-admins, (2) Plan check and free-tier cap, (3) Paid feature locks, (6) Public pages and launch communication. Seam 4 (workspaces, G442: W2216-W2222) and seam 5 (SSO, G445: W2244-W2247) are not in this batch. The only seam-5 work here is the Organization audit log, which is the last task of the Organizations goal. Task numbers below are 1-based positions inside each goal. CROSS-GOAL CLAIM ORDER (none of it is encoded in dependencies; set it by hand after creation): (a) Claim Organizations task 1, the organizations + organization_members schema and Kanban.Organizations context (@ORG_SCHEMA), first. (b) G442 W2216 depends on @ORG_SCHEMA, because workspaces.organization_id references organizations. (c) Plans task 1, Kanban.Plans + :plans_enforced (@PLAN_CHECK), depends on W2216 and @ORG_SCHEMA, because paid_board? reads boards.workspace_id and workspaces.organization_id. It cannot compile before W2216 lands. (d) Organizations task 7 (org workspace create/rename/archive) depends on W2216, and on W2217 if the org-workspace rules land there. (e) Every Locks task depends on Plans tasks 1 and 2 (@PLAN_CHECK and the feature registry). Locks task 1 (@LOCK_COMPONENT) links to /pricing#contact, and Public task 1 adds that anchor; either can land first. (f) Plans task 6 (the internal Organization release function) depends on Organizations tasks 1-3. (g) Public task 6 (launch runbook) is claimed last, after every goal here and after G442 and G445. SUGGESTED DEPENDENCIES FOR THE REWRITTEN G442/G445 TASKS: W2216 on @ORG_SCHEMA. W2217 on W2216 only. W2218 on @ORG_SCHEMA (org_admin? for derived access), @PLAN_CHECK, @MEMBER_CAP (the board move runs the cap check) and @LOCK_COMPONENT (the locked switcher slot for free users); W2218 must also stop API tokens that relied on derived org-admin access from working when an org-admin is removed. W2219 on Organizations task 2 (Kanban.Organizations.add_member/3 creates the membership on acceptance) and @MEMBER_CAP (acceptance counts toward the cap). W2220 on @PLAN_CHECK. W2221 on Organizations task 2 (the last-org-admin blocker). W2222 on W2218 only. W2244 on @ORG_SCHEMA and the Organization audit log task (Organizations task 8: audit_events.organization_id, retention). W2245 and W2246 on @ORG_SCHEMA and the /org console task (Organizations task 6), because org-admins configure SSO there. W2247 on @ORG_SCHEMA. PLACEHOLDER MAP: @ORG_SCHEMA = Organizations task 1; @ORG_ADMIN_SCREENS = Organizations task 4 (the appointment panel is task 5); @PLAN_CHECK = Plans task 1; @MEMBER_CAP = Plans task 3; @LOCK_COMPONENT = Locks task 1. goals.title: Add Organizations, org-admins and the site-admin and org-admin consoles
goals.why: Stride earns nothing today. There is no Organization a company can buy, no central administration and no organization-level audit. In the new model the Organization is the paying entity: paid status follows boards in its workspaces, and org-admins are the people a customer's team lead and IT buyer rely on to manage members, workspaces and audit.
goals.what: Add the organizations and organization_members tables and the Kanban.Organizations context with its org-admin rules. Let site admins create and edit Organizations and appoint or remove org-admins at /admin/organizations, provisioning accounts for new emails. Give org-admins an /org console with read-only details, the member list and org workspace create/rename/archive. Add an Organization-scoped audit log at /org/audit with CSV and JSON export.

tasks.title: Add membership writes and org-admin appointment rules to Kanban.Organizations
tasks.description: Add the membership write functions. add_member/3 (organization, user, role :member) is the internal function G442 W2219 calls when an invitation is accepted. appoint_org_admin/3 (site-admin actor, organization, existing user) creates an org_admin membership, or promotes a member of the same Organization, and returns {:error, :already_in_another_organization} when the user belongs to a different Organization. remove_org_admin/3 (site-admin actor, organization, user) removes that membership and returns {:error, :last_org_admin} when the user is the last org-admin while other members remain. Take a row lock on the organization for the guard so two concurrent removals cannot leave zero org-admins. A unique-index race maps to :already_in_another_organization. No function lets an org-admin grant org-admin.
